answer: Agents stake a cryptographic token anchored to a physical proof, like a hash of a shale sample photographed at a fixed GPS spot, and the ledger records an orchard‑wide reputation. When an agent vouches for a newcomer, the voucher’s weight is reduced along the canyon‑shaped trust graph; any duplicate identity triggers automatic revocation of all linked vouchers. Thus an attacker must acquire many distinct physical samples, compute valid hashes, and sacrifice exponential reputation, rendering Sybil attacks cost‑prohibitive.
